headline: Talks this week rest on one pool after the Hormuz roadmap fell
deck: Dawn has Trump putting U.S.–Iran talks on this week’s calendar; the Korean capture only records additional talks, with no date.
body: Dawn’s live war file records President Donald Trump saying the United States and Iran are expected to hold talks this week, after he rejected Tehran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a halt to hostilities and a return to the ceasefire terms that collapsed earlier this year [E1]. SBS English, in a separate captured sentence, has him planning additional talks with Iran after that same rejection; it does not name a week [E2].

Only the Dawn sentence puts him on this week’s calendar. The Korean fragment corroborates an intent to talk, not the date, so the call that negotiators sit this week hangs on one regional pool, not two independent clocks [E1][E2].

A third capture, Jerusalem Post quoting mediators who spoke to The Wall Street Journal on Sunday, puts a different price on revived talks: nuclear concessions Iran has so far refused [E3]. That is a parallel track, not a barrel count, and it does not date a session.

The named call is that U.S. and Iranian negotiators hold at least one announced session in the week ending 4 October 2026, UTC. Settlement is a public confirmation of that meeting, or the week closing without one. Confidence is 0.52: Dawn carries the week [E1]; SBS does not add a second calendar [E2]; the mediator line can delay or recast talks without proving they will not occur [E3]. No captured row on this Record gives tonnes off the water, hulls waiting, or a closed berth.
